in_text_mentions: The site of onset of symptoms is usually the abdomen, often within striae distensae and with an intensely pruritic urticarial rash with erythematous, edematous papules, and plaques (Figure 3). Sparing of the umbilical region is a characteristic finding. The disease spreads to other body sites such as proximal thighs, buttocks, and the back. Rarely the eruption spreads ideally involving arms and legs [9]. The morphology changes while the disease advances, developing polymorphic features such as papulovesicles, erythema, and annular wheals.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: H&E punch biopsy from case of polymorphic eruption of pregnancy with bullae formation. Disease attribution via disease-focused article title plus captioned vesicle/edema manifestation and workup for PUPPP; in-text provides perivascular lymphohistiocytic inflammation supporting vocabulary finding. Vesicle/bullae formation is unusual for PUPPP, hence atypical. B: Higher magnification x10 view of same PUPPP biopsy showing intraepidermal/subcorneal vesicle with eosinophils/lymphocytes. In-text perivascular lymphohistiocytic inflammation supports vocabulary histology finding. Bullous/vesicular histology is atypical for PUPPP. C: x20 view of same PUPPP biopsy showing vesicle-associated eosinophils/lymphocytes and dermal edema. Vocabulary finding supported by in-text perivascular inflammation description for Fig 2. Vesicle formation in PUPPP is atypical bullous presentation.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Pregnant abdomen with erythematous urticoid papules coalescing into plaques with thigh spread in article titled polymorphic eruption of pregnancy / PUPPP; panel-specific caption supports PUPPP morphology. B: Right lateral trunk shows same scattered erythematous urticoid papules/plaques described in caption for PUPPP/polymorphic eruption of pregnancy case. C: Right upper arm shows erythematous urticoid papules/plaques as captioned for PUPPP/polymorphic eruption of pregnancy case. D: Bilateral legs show erythematous papules/plaques with spread to lower extremities as captioned for PUPPP/polymorphic eruption of pregnancy case.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is H&E histology from PEP/PUPPP case showing superficial and mid-dermal inflammatory infiltrate, matching perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate vocabulary; disease attribution supported by PEP diagnosis in-text and disease-focused title. B: Panel B is H&E histology from same PEP/PUPPP biopsy; perivascular infiltrate visible histologically, with caption-described spongiosis and papillary dermal edema recorded as proposed findings. C: Panel C high-power histology shows lymphocytes and eosinophils, directly supporting perivascular lymphocytes with eosinophils synonym for PUPPP histology in PEP-diagnosed case.
panels.attribution_text: Moschella et al. Polymorphic eruption of pregnancy successfully treated with dupilumab in the postpartum period: A case report.. SAGE open medical case reports 2026. doi:10.1177/2050313x261446055. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Superficial and mid-dermal inflammatory infiltrate (magnification ×40 (a)); epidermal spongiosis and papillary dermal edema (magnification ×100 (b)); and the inflammatory infiltrate consists of lymphocytes and eosinophils (magnification ×200 (c)).

No evidence of a subepidermal blister or eosinophilic tagging along the basement membrane was identified (Figure 2). Direct immunofluorescence was negative. Given the morphology of pruritic urticoid papules with onset shortly before delivery and worsening thereafter, a diagnosis of PEP was made. Intense pruritus and widespread distribution of the rash warranted systemic treatment. Prednisone was contraindicated given her gestational diabetes and gestational hypertension.
